specific_finding: 2 Samuel 3:2-3 explicitly includes Absalom among sons born to David, and 13:1 says Absalom son of David. These direct statements confirm the sonship that 15:7-14 shows through the father, king and David narrative sequence.

units.complete_text: Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam the Jezreelite;
his second was Daluia, by Abigail the Carmelite; and the third was Absalom son of Maacah, daughter of Talmai king of Geshur;
the fourth was Ornia son of Phengith; and the fifth was Sabatia, by Abital;
and the sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, David’s wife. These were born to David in Hebron.
After this, Absalom son of David had a sister very beautiful in appearance, named Tamar, and Amnon son of David loved her.
At the end of forty years, Absalom said to his father, “Please let me go to Hebron and fulfill the vows I made to the Lord.
Your servant made a vow while I was living at Geshur in Syria: ‘If the Lord indeed brings me back to Jerusalem, I will worship the Lord.’”
The king said to him, “Go in peace.” He rose and went to Hebron.
Absalom sent spies throughout all Israel’s tribes, saying, “When you hear the horn’s sound, say, ‘King Absalom has begun to reign in Hebron!’”
Two hundred invited men went with Absalom from Jerusalem. They went in their simplicity and knew nothing of the matter.
While sacrificing, Absalom sent and summoned Ahithophel the Gelmonite, David’s counselor, from his city Gola. The conspiracy grew strong, and the people with Absalom kept increasing.
A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel have gone after Absalom.”

David said to all his servants with him in Jerusalem, “Rise, let us flee, for we have no deliverance from Absalom. Hurry to leave, lest he hurry and overtake us, thrust calamity upon us, and strike the city with the sword’s edge.”
